All five judge files were parsed; their judge tables contain only judge/mode/timeout/isolated/prompt_template/mcp_servers and retain judge = "claude-code" at line 2, with no model, reasoning_effort, temperature or judge-level weight. All 15 configured-inspection test-source hashes and all 37 verification-local source hashes match current frozen bytes. The parser observation selects the specified judge/model for all five dimensions and confirms installed Claude Code 2.1.281 and Playwright MCP 0.0.79. Its driver explicitly supplies the environment and substitutes /usr/bin/true for provider execution; therefore it proves local discovery/argument construction, not Harbor credential expansion, live authentication or a completed grade. No provider call was made by this reviewer. Missing full grading remains outside this row's configuration verdict and must not be waived for runtime-clearance rows.
counterexample: Static adversarial analysis: a broken submitted app could try to place a weak-model judge.toml under /app/tests or alter inherited REWARDKIT_MODEL to obtain an easier evaluator. This does not supply a counterexample to the inspected wiring: only /app and /assets transfer (task.toml:2), the verifier copies its own /tests with root-only permissions (tests/Dockerfile:43-44), and test.sh:207-208 discovers absolute /tests/<suite>. The app itself starts with env -i and uid/gid 65534 (test.sh:104-111), so changing its process environment does not change the parent judge configuration. This app attack was considered from source, not executed or scored. A conforming alternative using public CDN assets with the expected judge fallback must not fail merely because no allowlist exists; task.toml:37-38 explicitly permits public networking. Likewise isolated = false within the judge table is the prescribed browser-sharing setting and does not negate the separate verifier environment. No row-10 false acceptance or false rejection was established.
